newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: North Korea sells opium to fund party, defector says.
newsitem.headline: North Korea sells opium to fund party, defector says.

text.p: North Korea is helping to finance its ruling Workers' Party through drug money by exporting opium, a military pharmicist who defected to the South said on Monday.
"Opium is produced in about 10 places in North Korea," Huh Chang-gul, 47, who arrived with his 17-year-old daughter on October 28, told a news conference.
He said raw opium from poppies grown on the farms was shipped to a pharmaceutical factory in Chungjin, northeast of Pyongyang, for processing.
The refined product was exported. "The money from opium exports is used by the ruling party as operating funds," Huh told reporters.
North Korea's foreign trade has collapsed and the country is desperately short of foreign currency.
Huh also said the North Korean military was rehearsing an invasion of the South in areas topographically similar to South Korea.
"Exercises for attacking South Korea are conducted in South Pyong-An province and North Hwang-Hae province, whose geographical conditions are similar to those of South Korea," he said.
South and North Korea have been technically at war since the 1950-53 Korean conflict ended in a truce.
